source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 3 (ISL A3) · lesson 17. Rewritten for children from Dr. Hassan's lesson; facts and references kept.
topic: Good news for Ibrahim and Sarah

learn.en: Ibrahim and his wife Sārah were old and had no children together.
learn.title: An old couple

learn.en: Guests came to Ibrahim's home. He hurried to honour them with a roasted calf. They didn't eat — they were angels! They said: “Do not be afraid.” (Qur'an 11:69–70)
learn.title: Special guests

learn.en: The angels gave Sārah the good news of a son, Isḥāq, and after him a grandson, Yaʿqūb. (Qur'an 11:71)
learn.title: Good news!

learn.en: Sārah was amazed: “Shall I have a child when I am old?” The angels said: “Do you wonder at Allah's decree? Allah's mercy and blessings are upon you.” (Qur'an 11:72–73)
learn.title: Nothing is too hard for Allah

learn.en: Isḥāq became a prophet, and so did his son Yaʿqūb. Many prophets came from Yaʿqūb's family.
learn.title: A family of prophets

quiz.en: What good news did Sārah receive?
opts: A son, Isḥāq, and a grandson, Yaʿqūb

quiz.en: True or false? Ibrahim hurried to honour his guests.
True or false? Some things are too hard for Allah.

think.q: How can you honour a guest who visits your home?
think.a: Welcome them with a smile, offer them something to eat or drink, and let them sit comfortably — like Ibrahim did.

parents.summary: Ibrahim honoured his guests, who were angels. They brought Sārah, in old age, the good news of Isḥāq and Yaʿqūb — both prophets. Nothing is too hard for Allah.
parents.tip: Next time guests come, let your child serve them first.
